state.persona: Matt, trip organizer, privacy-aware parent. Planning Lisbon for himself, partner Sam, daughter Lily (7). Built his profile from his Spotify listening.
state.job: Invite friends to vote on the trip without oversharing personal details.
state.visible_text: Panel 'BRING THE CREW': 'The whole trip travels inside the link, so there's no sign-up. Friends vote on their own phone and send their picks back with one tap.' [Invite people] 'Link copied. Paste it in the group chat.' Footnote: 'Anyone with the link can see the plan and who's going (names, kids' ages, home city). Music taste stays on your device. Picks sync when a link is opened, not live.'
state.what_the_link_actually_contains: Every traveler's name, adult/kid, the kid's exact age (7), each traveler's interest tags (e.g. Matt: food, music, nightlife), hometown 'New York', dates, every idea card including cards generated from Matt's music taste with blurbs 'Because you listen to hip hop, trap.' and '40% of your top songs are from before 2000, and rock is in your mix.', everyone's existing votes (who loved/passed what), and the organizer's name. The raw Spotify taste object itself is removed. The link is a URL fragment, not sent to the server, but anyone it is forwarded to can decode it.

disclosure_adequate.instructions: How adequate is the footnote as a disclosure of what the link actually reveals?

expects_taste_hidden.instructions: Probability Matt, after reading 'Music taste stays on your device', believes friends who open the link will NOT see anything about what music he listens to.

surprised_by_blurb.instructions: Probability Matt would be unhappy or surprised to learn a friend's phone shows 'Because you listen to hip hop, trap.' and '40% of your top songs are from before 2000' from his link.
